meta.title: Adapdev — bespoke software for Australian small business
meta.description: ADMS is a document management system for Australian sole traders, small businesses and law firms. On your hardware, integrated with Office, no subscription.

cards.title: Save from Word lands in the right matter
cards.description: The Word, Outlook, Excel and PowerPoint add-ins add File → Save to ADMS. One prompt for the client and matter, one click, and the file is versioned and audited.

cards.title: Your office network becomes a shared archive
cards.description: Multi-person deployments share one ADMS database. Permissions per client, per matter, per document type. Every read, write and delete logged with who, when and from where.

cards.title: The subscription you don't pay
cards.description: ADMS is a one-off licence per installation. No per-seat fee, no per-document charge, no cloud bill that arrives in US dollars. The data lives on hardware you already own.

how.title: Four steps, nothing hidden on your drive
how.body: ADMS runs locally. There is no account to create, no sign-up form, no server you can't log into. Install, point it at your folders, and you are filing within ten minutes.

steps.title: Install
steps.description: The signed server installer stands up the API, creates the dedicated service account, and provisions the database on SQLite or SQL Server.
steps.imageAlt: Light radiating from a single point

steps.title: Point
steps.description: Drag the folder of existing documents onto the desktop client. ADMS reads them, files them under their client, and makes everything searchable.

steps.title: Save
steps.description: The Office add-ins add File → Save to ADMS. Pick a client and matter, hit Enter, done. The file is versioned and the audit log records who filed it.

steps.title: Find
steps.description: Full-text search across every document. Filter by client, matter, document type, author or date. Open in the native application with one click.
steps.imageAlt: Two surfaces meeting at an edge

card.text: We reply the same working day.

items.a: On your hardware. The server installer creates a SQLite database (sole-trader install, one laptop) or configures a SQL Server database (small-business or law-firm install, one on-site server). ADMS never ships your documents to Adapdev, Microsoft, Amazon, or anyone else. There is no SaaS backend to switch off.

items.q: What happens if we outgrow the laptop install?
items.a: The data migrates. The sole-trader SQLite database can be imported straight into a small-business SQL Server install with a bundled tool — clients, matters, documents, permissions, audit log, the lot. You don't lose a filing when you add staff.

items.q: Does it work with the Office we already have?
items.a: Yes. The desktop installer adds native add-ins to Word, Outlook, Excel and PowerPoint. Microsoft 365, Office 2021 or Office 2019 are all supported. There is no cloud sign-in step; the add-ins talk to the ADMS API on your own network.

items.q: Our existing filing is a mess — is that a dealbreaker?
items.a: No, and it is usually the reason to start. Drop the current folder structure on the desktop client; ADMS imports what's there, surfaces the duplicates, and gives you a clean filing scheme to fix the mess once rather than every day.

items.q: What about backup and disaster recovery?
items.a: ADMS does not replace your backup strategy, and it doesn't try to. The sole-trader SQLite database is one file — copy it. The small-business SQL Server database runs on your own server — use the backup tooling you already have, or the scripted job the installer ships. The installer prints a recovery runbook you can hand to IT.
Adapdev directly. There is no first-tier queue — the person who shipped the release is the person who answers the bug report. We're a small shop; see the About page.
